'''Apex Gaming''' was previously a North American team. In September 2016, they merged with {{bl|Team Dignitas}}. For the Apex Legends esports wiki, '''[[apex:Main Page|click here]]'''.

== History ==
=== 2016 Season ===
'''Apex Gaming''' was announced to have acquired [[Team Imagine]]'s [[NA Challenger Series/2016 Season/Spring Season|NACS 2016 Spring Season]] seed in a LoL Esports article on January 8, 2016.<ref>[http://www.lolesports.com/en_US/articles/2016-na-cs-qualifier-finals-primer 2016 NA CS Qualifier Finals primer] ''lolesports.com''</ref> Their roster wasn't revealed until almost two weeks later and included three former LCS players - [[Cris]], [[Keane]], and [[Xpecial]] - and two Korean players: [[Eve]] from [[Samsung]] and [[Police (Park Hyeong-gi)|Police]] from [[ESC Ever|Ever]], with [[Shrimp]] as a substitute. They were coached by former [[Team Coast]] coach [[Saintvicious]] and former Samsung mid laner [[BlisS]].<ref name="formation">[http://www.twitlonger.com/show/n_1so78if Saintvicious's Twitlonger] ''twitlonger.com''</ref>

Apex won both the regular season of NACS and the [[NA Challenger Series/2016 Season/Spring Playoffs|playoffs]], using both Eve and Shrimp actively in the jungle. In the [[League Championship Series/North America/2016 Season/Summer Promotion|promotion tournament]], they were seeded first against the ninth-place [[Team Impulse]], to whom they lost, and then against second place Challenger team [[Team Dragon Knights]], a rematch of the Challenger Series finals. This time, they didn't even drop one game against TDK and qualified successfully for the [[League Championship Series/North America/2016 Season/Summer Season|LCS summer split]].

On May 2, during the midseason break, Apex announced the indefinite suspension of Eve for "disciplinary reasons."<ref name="evesuspend">[http://twitter.com/apxgg/status/727061105529511937 Apex's Tweet] ''twitter.com''</ref> Soon after the suspension, ESPN reported that the reason for the ban was due to Eve's Korean account being banned by Riot Korea for use of scripts.<ref>[http://espn.go.com/espn/now?nowId=21-0519272063513401574-4 Jacob Wolf's ESPN Now post] ''espn.go.com''</ref> Additionally, the team added [[Ray]] and [[Apollo (Apollo Price)|Apollo]] to their starting roster, replacing Cris and Police, respectively. The starting lineup of Ray, Shrimp, Keane, Apollo, and Xpecial was used for all of their summer split games.

Apex's season started out strong, with a 2-0 first week including a 2-1 upset of reigning NA LCS champions and [[2016 Mid-Season Invitational|MSI]] alums [[Counter Logic Gaming|CLG]]. Their success, however, was short-lived, and by week 5 they were in 7th place, where they remained for the rest of the season, out of reach of the [[League Championship Series/North America/2016 Season/Summer Playoffs|playoffs]] but also safe from [[League Championship Series/North America/2017 Season/Spring Promotion|relegations]] for the [[League Championship Series/North America/2017 Season/Spring Season|2017 Spring Season]].

In September, Apex Gaming was acquired by the '''Philadelphia 76ers''' along with Team Dignitas, and the two organizations merged, under the Dignitas brand.<ref name="76acquire">[http://team-dignitas.net/articles/news/Team-Dignitas/10251/philadelphia-76ers-acquire-merge-and-manage-leading-esports-teams-dignitas-and-apex Philadelphia 76ers acquire, merge and manage leading esports teams Dignitas and Apex] ''team-dignitas.net''</ref>
